clue.text: This may rise to a high figure

definitions.text: This may rise to a high figure

parts.words: This may rise to a high figure
parts.note: a tall pillar rising to carry a statue, like Nelson's in Trafalgar Square, with a figure at its top

explanation.walkthrough: The 'high figure' sounds like a large number rising, but it is a statue standing on top of a tall pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument pillar is built upward to support a statue set high above the street.

clue.text: Breaker of the law ?.

parts.note: a breaker is also a big sea wave, so a wave of law-breaking is a surge in offences

explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaker of the law' looks like a criminal, but a breaker is also a wave, here a wave of offences.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden spate of offending is likened to a big sea wave, which is also called a breaker.

clue.text: As a vessel, it's matchless

explanation.definitionFit: A barge used to unload ships is one sense; the other is a pocket flame-maker that needs no matches.

clue.text: Is writing following the style, or its peculiarities ?

indicators.note: the words before it come after the style in the answer

parts.note: style means manner, a way of doing something
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A critic asks whether a writer's copying of a style shows only its oddities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' is the charade signal: the style comes first in the answer, then 'Is' and 'writing' after it. The definition is the clue's last words.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitual quirks of behaviour or style are a person's or a style's peculiarities.

clue.text: B.A. who gets a kick out of life?

definitions.text: B.A. who gets a kick out of life?

parts.words: B.A. who gets a kick out of life?
parts.note: B and A make up half of the word back, and a footballer in that position kicks the ball for a living

explanation.walkthrough: 'B.A.' looks like a graduate, but the letters are half of BACK; a football player in that position gets his kicks for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: A defensive midfield football player, named after his position, spends his working life kicking a ball.

clue.text: There sounds much meaning in the plot

indicators.note: the phrase is said aloud and heard as another word

parts.note: much is a lot and meaning is meant, so the phrase gives a lot meant

explanation.surface: A reader feels the story's plot carries a lot of significance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much meaning' gives A LOT MEANT, which spoken is ALLOTMENT; 'There' and 'in the' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A rented patch of ground for growing vegetables is a garden plot.

clue.text: Not how the guilty payer describes it

definitions.text: Not how the guilty payer describes it

parts.words: Not how the guilty payer describes it
parts.note: someone ordered to pay a penalty would not call it excellent or all right, which is the other sense of the word

explanation.walkthrough: The word for a court's money penalty also means 'all right', which is the last thing the person paying would say about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A money penalty shares its spelling with the adjective for good, which the offender would never call it.

clue.text: Name-change one, found in the garden

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who changed their name became a different person, one spotted in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges NAME and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind-flower is a plant grown in garden beds.

clue.text: High-ups get half the takings

indicators.note: about half of the word takings is its last part, which is taken out

explanation.surface: Those at the top claim a half share of the earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the back part of TAKINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Monarchs are the people at the very top of society.

clue.text: Spirit obtainable in imperial pints

indicators.note: the letters can be got from inside the word imperial

explanation.surface: Drinks are sold in old imperial pint measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' looks like a drink beside 'pints', but it is a fairy of Persian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a fairy-like being from Persian mythology, a kind of spirit.

clue.text: So innocent, the subject of a genuine reform

definitions.note: such an innocent person, a noun phrase

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are given a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone so naive becomes the object of a genuine attempt at reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges GENUINE; 'the subject of a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An artless young woman, especially as a stage role, is such an innocent.

clue.text: Doesn't necessarily describe the jaw of a night watchman

definitions.text: Doesn't necessarily describe the jaw of a night watchman

parts.words: Doesn't necessarily describe the jaw of a night watchman
parts.note: a long, hollow-cheeked jaw has a name taken from the light a night watchman carries

explanation.walkthrough: The light a night watchman carries also describes a long, gaunt jaw, but his own jaw need not be like that.
explanation.definitionFit: A long thin jaw is named after the light carried by watchmen, though the watchman needn't have one.

clue.text: They have no mean policies

parts.note: mean here is the middle or average point, which radicals reject

explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' reads as stingy, but it is the average or middle position, which radicals never take.
explanation.definitionFit: Radicals hold views far from the political centre, the mean.

clue.text: Records with which one may be lumbered?

definitions.text: with which one may be lumbered?

explanation.definitionFit: Records are entries in a ship's diary; timber cut into lengths is lumber you may be lumbered with.

clue.text: Where numbers take part in a love game ?

definitions.text: Where numbers take part in a love game

parts.words: Where numbers take part in a love game
parts.note: the numbers are the game of fives, and court is to woo, so a courting game where fives is played

explanation.walkthrough: Fives is a British handball game; its playing area is a court, and to court is to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Fives is a British handball game played in a walled court; courting is a love game.

clue.text: Form of transport vital for a diver ?

explanation.definitionFit: A company flying passengers is a form of transport; a hose feeding breath to a diver is vital to them.

clue.text: Odd style Anne brought to melodrama

indicators.note: the letters are put into an odd, unusual order

explanation.surface: A woman named Anne brings a strange flair to a dramatic stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges STYLE ANNE. EAST LYNNE is a Victorian sensation novel by Mrs Henry Wood, famous in its stage versions.
explanation.definitionFit: This Victorian tale was best known as a tear-jerking stage show of the old sensational kind.

clue.text: Cardinally lofty

parts.note: a cardinal is addressed as His Eminence, so high in the manner of one

explanation.walkthrough: Cardinals are styled 'His Eminence', so being lofty in a cardinal's way gives the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinguished people stand high; a cardinal's title, His Eminence, comes from the same word.

clue.text: A lot of sound hats needing repair

indicators.note: the letters are broken and must be mended into a new order

explanation.surface: Many hard hats still in good shape are due to be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing repair' rearranges SOUND HATS.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast number, many hundreds of hundreds, is a great many.

clue.text: Arithmetical problems are bound to take him aback

indicators.note: the words are read backwards, taken in the opposite direction

parts.note: arithmetic problems set in class are sums

explanation.surface: Maths puzzles are sure to take a person by surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aback' turns the whole run of letters round. The definition is just 'him', meaning the Dutch Renaissance scholar, a thin definition typical of older clues.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun stands for a man, here the Renaissance Dutch humanist scholar.

clue.text: But it's not a contest for fly-weights

definitions.text: But it's not a contest for fly-weights

parts.words: But it's not a contest for fly-weights
parts.note: flyweights are light boxers, but here the fury belongs to flying passengers

explanation.walkthrough: 'fly-weights' looks like boxers, and a 'contest' a fight, but it means passengers who fly losing their tempers on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers' fury on a plane is a flare-up among those flying, not a boxing bout.

clue.text: Musical effect produced by playing quavers ?

definitions.text: Musical effect produced by playing quavers

parts.words: Musical effect produced by playing quavers
parts.note: quavers are short notes but also trembles, and the effect is a trembling of the note

explanation.walkthrough: 'quavers' look like eighth notes, but to quaver is to tremble, which is what this effect does.
explanation.definitionFit: A wavering repetition of a note is a musical effect that makes the sound tremble.

clue.text: From Cairo an unusual instrument

indicators.note: the letters are given an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd musical instrument has come from the Egyptian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges CAIRO AN; 'From' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A small egg-shaped clay flute is a wind instrument.

clue.text: But this hole can be on either side of the boat

definitions.text: But this hole can be on either side of the boat

parts.words: But this hole can be on either side of the boat
parts.note: a round window in a ship's hull is named after the left side, yet is found on both

explanation.walkthrough: The ship's left side shares its name with the round windows in the hull, which nonetheless appear on the right side too.
explanation.definitionFit: The left side of a ship gives its name to the round windows, which sit on both sides.

clue.text: Are its airs always so soft?

definitions.text: Are its airs always so soft?

parts.words: Are its airs always so soft?
parts.note: the keyboard instrument shares its name with the musical direction for soft

explanation.walkthrough: The keyboard instrument's name is also the Italian direction for playing softly, yet it does not always play quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: The keyboard instrument shares its name with the Italian marking meaning softly.

clue.text: Not members, of a poor government

definitions.text: Not members, of a poor government

parts.words: Not members, of a poor government
parts.note: rule by the wealthy is the opposite of rule by the poor

explanation.walkthrough: Rule by the rich, so its rulers could never belong to a government of poor people.
explanation.definitionFit: The wealthy rulers of a state run by riches are the reverse of any government of the poor.

clue.text: The end of time

parts.note: the word means both a limit or end and a fixed period of time

explanation.walkthrough: The word is both a fixed period of time and that period's limit or end.
explanation.definitionFit: A school or legal session is a period of time, and the word also means a boundary or end.

clue.text: She's no catch ?

parts.note: an unmarried woman's title is also the word for failing to make a catch

explanation.walkthrough: The title for an unmarried woman is also what a fielder does who drops the ball, so she is 'no catch'.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried young woman's title doubles as a failure to catch the ball.

clue.text: Literary nights

parts.note: the famous story collection is the Thousand and One Nights, known by a regional name

explanation.walkthrough: The story collection of Scheherazade is called the 'Arabian Nights', so the adjective describes these literary nights.
explanation.definitionFit: The great story collection told by Scheherazade is known in English by the name of its region.

clue.text: With difficulty I run one get-together.

indicators.note: the letters are forced with difficulty into a new order

explanation.surface: An organiser complains that running a single party is hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With difficulty' rearranges I RUN ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of old friends or relatives is a meeting together again.

clue.text: Man of superior vision?

parts.note: a supervisor watches from above, so his sight is superior in position, not quality

explanation.walkthrough: 'superior vision' suggests sharp eyesight, but this man sees from a higher rank as he watches over workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor looks over the work of others from a superior post.

clue.text: People of standing take them in hand

definitions.text: People of standing take them in hand

parts.words: People of standing take them in hand
parts.note: standing passengers on buses and trains hold the loops hanging from the ceiling

explanation.walkthrough: 'People of standing' sounds like VIPs, but these are commuters standing on a train who hold on to loops.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging loops on buses and trains are held by passengers who must stand.
